content:
The Texas governor's race came to the Gateway City on Tuesday. Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic nominee for governor, stopped in Laredo as part of a get-out-the-vote push, meeting supporters and asking — in Spanish — for their votes, according to KGNS.

Hinojosa is challenging Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who is seeking a fourth term in the November 3 election. Her Laredo stop is part of a broader Democratic effort to mobilize voters in South Texas, a region both parties are courting hard after Webb County backed a Republican for president in 2024 for the first time in more than a century.

The visit lands squarely in the middle of early voting, which runs in Webb County through October 30 across 14 polling sites. With the governor's race sharing the ballot with a full local slate — mayor, four council seats, municipal judge — the GOTV math is simple: turnout decides it.

What to watch: whether the statewide campaigns keep showing up in Laredo over the final two weeks, and whether Webb County's early-vote numbers move. We'll be tracking both.
